run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T16:58:29Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by HTTP 504s generated by frontend-proxy's own 15 s upstream response timeout on the recommendation path, not by errors in frontend-proxy itself. In the 16:58:00-17:10:00 window frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans carry 55.44 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans against 5111.47 STATUS_CODE_UNSET, while its 'router frontend egress' client spans carry 0 errors; access logs show '504 UT response_timeout ... 15000' only for GET /api/recommendations while /api/checkout and /api/products returned 200. A complete trace shows the chain load-generator user_get_recommendations -> frontend-proxy ingress 504 (15.001 s) -> frontend GET /api/recommendations 200 in 15.342 s -> frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations in 15.339 s with gRPC status 0. The deepest cause the evidence supports is CPU starvation of the recommendation service: recommendation container CPU rose from ~0.011-0.013 cores to ~0.096 cores (its limit is 100m) at 16:56-16:58 and its CFS throttling ratio rose from ~5% to 96-98%, while its request rate did not increase; all other otel-demo pods stayed at <=24% throttling. Recommendation's own spans stop at ~16:57 and its logs stop at 17:03:33, so its internals during the incident are not observable. Why its CPU demand rose ~8x per request is not determinable with the available data (change history is not integrated), so the trigger behind the CPU surge remains an open hypothesis.

claims.text: Over 16:58:00-17:10:00, frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans recorded 55.44 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans versus 5111.47 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans, a ratio of about 1.1% of ingress spans.

frontend-proxy error spans are confined to span_name="ingress"; its client span_name="router frontend egress" recorded 0 error spans at every sample in 16:00-17:10 while ingress errors rose. At 17:05, ingress ERROR was 31.11 per 5m against 2608.89 per 5m UNSET, and egress ERROR was 0 against 2642.22 per 5m UNSET.

The frontend-proxy ingress error burst began at ~16:59: the 5-minute error increase went 0 (16:57), 7.78 (16:59), 28.89 (17:01), 43.33 (17:02), 44.44 (17:04), then 18.89 (17:07), 5.18 (17:09) and 0 at the 17:10 sample; isolated 1-2 span blips also appear from ~16:38.

A complete trace (3761ca9dd7eb387d96ebefddcd0680f0) shows: load-generator user_get_recommendations 15.158 s -> load-generator GET 504 15.157 s -> frontend-proxy ingress 504 15.001 s -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' 15.001 s with error="true", http.status_code="0" -> frontend GET 200 in 15.001 s -> frontend 'GET /api/recommendations' 200 in 15.342 s -> frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations 15.339 s with rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

That same trace returned all 17 spans (spans_omitted 0, spans_outside_window 0) and contains no span whose service is recommendation, even though the frontend's ListRecommendations client span and product-catalog spans are present.

frontend-proxy access logs record 'GET /api/recommendations?productIds=... 504 UT response_timeout ... 15000' while 'POST /api/checkout' and 'GET /api/products/...' returned 200 in the same minutes; some /api/recommendations requests did return 200 but after 5945-9506 ms.

Recommendation calls measured on the frontend side became slow but stayed under 15 s: for span grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations, the le="10000.0" count fell below the le="+Inf" count during the burst (e.g. 40.0 vs 69.33 at 17:02, 57.33 vs 94.67 at 17:03) while le="15000.0" equalled le="+Inf" at every step, and the per-2m call count stayed roughly 40-47/min.

The recommendation container's CPU usage was 0.0108-0.0133 cores at every 2-minute sample from 16:34:29 to 16:54:29, then 0.0574 at 16:56:29 and 0.0967 at 16:58:29, holding ~0.095 cores afterwards; the container's CPU limit is 100m.
The recommendation pod's CFS throttled-periods ratio was 0.042-0.061 through 16:54:29, then 0.630 at 16:56:29, 0.976 at 16:58:29 and 0.96-0.98 through the 17:06:29 sample.

At 17:05 the recommendation pod was throttled 0.9645 of CFS periods at 0.0926 cores, while the highest throttle ratio among all other otel-demo pods was cart 0.2371, frontend 0.2310, postgresql 0.2256, product-catalog 0.1947 and frontend-proxy 0.0317.

Deployment recommendation in otel-demo has 1 replica (1 ready, 1 available), image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-recommendation, container recommendation with limits cpu 100m/memory 160Mi and requests cpu 30m/memory 80Mi; its ReplicaSet recommendation-5f45f75855 is owned by Deployment recommendation.
The recommendation pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv is Running and ready with restart count 0 and no previous container instance, and was started at 2026-11-16T16:17:06Z.

The recommendation service's own span metrics stop at the onset: its server span /oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations increased 66.67-92 per 2-minute step up to the 16:57 sample and 0 from the 16:58 sample onward, and before 16:57 le="10000.0" equalled le="+Inf" (all spans completed in under 10 s).
The newest recommendation container log line in the authorized window is at 2026-11-16T17:03:33.852054Z; the lines read are 'Receive ListRecommendations for product ids:[...]' messages.
The recommendation container's working set grew from ~42.1 MB before the onset to 55-60 MB afterwards, still well below its 160Mi memory limit.

At 16:55 (before the onset) recommendation served 511.58 ListRecommendations server spans per 10m, 511.58 get_product_list internal spans and 511.58 /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts client spans, all STATUS_CODE_UNSET with no error status.
The frontend service recorded 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans for every one of its operations across 16:35-17:09, and its pod ran at 0.0425 cores with a 0.2310 throttle ratio at 17:05.

product-catalog recorded 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, ran at 0.0067 cores with a 0.1947 throttle ratio at 17:05, and its spans inside the failing trace completed in 73-902 microseconds (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct) and 34 microseconds (ListProducts).
All otel-demo pods except frontend are scheduled on node i-07fdfccf76e0651ab, including recommendation, cart, product-catalog and frontend-proxy.

The flagd-config ConfigMap entry demo.flagd.json, read at ~17:12 (after the incident window), defines 12 ENABLED flags including recommendationCacheFailure and adHighCpu, all with defaultVariant "off".

Primary explanation: the recommendation service pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv became CPU-saturated at its 100m container limit and was throttled ~96-98% of CFS periods from ~16:56-16:58, which stretched ListRecommendations to 10-15 s; frontend's /api/recommendations route therefore exceeded frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream response timeout and Envoy returned 504 UT response_timeout, producing the frontend-proxy error spans that trigger RequestErrorRate.

Open sub-hypothesis for why CPU demand rose ~8x per request while the recommendation call rate stayed roughly flat: an in-process regression in demo:2.1.3-recommendation or a fault-injection flag (the config defines recommendationCacheFailure, which would force repeat work) could raise per-request CPU. The evidence cannot confirm which, because recommendation's own spans and logs stop at the onset and the flag state during the window is unverified.

Contributing configuration: the recommendation container's 100m CPU limit (request 30m) is what converts the elevated CPU demand into ~96% CFS throttling and multi-second latency; a larger CPU limit or additional replicas would have absorbed it.

recommendation was not down: its pod is Running and ready with 0 restarts and no previous container instance, and its ListRecommendations calls still returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0 (OK) at 15.3 s. The failure is latency-induced 504 at the proxy, not a crash or error response from recommendation, so pod readiness and its own error rate would not show the problem.

The flag snapshot taken at ~17:12 shows every flagd flag, including recommendationCacheFailure, with defaultVariant "off", so a flag-driven explanation is not established by the evidence (and the snapshot cannot prove the state during 16:56-17:10).

Node-wide or cluster-wide CPU contention is rejected as the driver: the other pods on the same node i-07fdfccf76e0651ab had throttle ratios of 0.2371 or less at 17:05 versus 0.9645 for recommendation, and frontend, product-catalog and frontend-proxy latencies stayed normal.
product-catalog is rejected as the latency source: it had 0 error spans, 0.0067 cores of CPU and 0.1947 throttling at 17:05, and its spans in the very trace that timed out took 34-902 microseconds.

frontend-proxy being unhealthy is rejected as the origin: it ran at 0.0112 cores with 0.0317 throttling at 17:05, its 'router frontend egress' client spans recorded 0 errors, and its access log shows the 504s are its own response_timeout (15000 ms) waiting on the frontend upstream.
Raise the recommendation container CPU limit above the current 100m (or add replicas) and re-measure per-request CPU, since the workload was throttled ~96-98% of periods at its limit.
Retrieve flagd flag change/audit history for 16:50-17:10 to establish whether recommendationCacheFailure (or another flag) was enabled during the window.

gaps: Recommendation's own spans stop at ~16:57 and its container log output stops at 17:03:33.852054Z, and the failing trace contains no recommendation span, so the internal breakdown of the 10-15 s (get_product_list vs /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts vs flagd ResolveBoolean) cannot be observed; recommendation latency after 16:58 is unknown rather than zero.

What raised recommendation's CPU demand ~8x at 16:56-16:58 is unknown: the change_history integration is not available, so I cannot verify whether the deployment resources, image digest, application config or flagd flag values changed at that time.
flagd flag values during the incident window are unverified; the ConfigMap read is a post-window snapshot (~17:12), and no flagd or flagd-ui log lines were returned for the window.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules returned no data for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and for type=alert, so the alert expression and denominator behind the reported 0.06666 value cannot be confirmed against the observed 55.44 error / 5111.47 UNSET ingress span counts.

No recommendation pod events were returned inside the window (events query for involvedObject name recommendation returned no data), so eviction/OOM cannot be positively excluded; restart count 0 and an absent previous container instance argue against a restart.

The recommendation log error search (filter error|exception|fail|panic|timeout|warn) returned no data for 16:40-17:10:54, so the absence of error lines in recommendation's logs is not proven; only the 'Receive ListRecommendations' lines were actually seen.

load-generator is not among the service_name values of traces_span_metrics_calls_total, so its 504 spans could not be counted from metrics and its request rate is only inferable from the frontend-side client spans.
next_steps: Profile or inspect the recommendation service inside the pod (CPU profile, GC, cache behaviour) against image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-recommendation to find the per-request CPU regression.

Review the frontend-proxy route timeout (15000000 microseconds / 15 s) and the frontend's gRPC deadline for /api/recommendations to decide whether a longer timeout or a latency-aware client is appropriate.
Add alerting on recommendation CFS throttling and on end-to-end /api/recommendations latency, so upstream 504s are not the first signal.
Confirm whether the recommendation Deployment's 100m CPU limit/30m request is intentional for this environment and adjust capacity accordingly.
Obtain flagd audit history or flagd-ui change log for 16:56-17:10 to test the recommendationCacheFailure hypothesis.
